newsitem.title: CHINA: Alcoa World starts China alumina delivery.
newsitem.headline: Alcoa World starts China alumina delivery.

text.p: The first shipment of alumina by Alcoa World Alumina and Chemicals to China National Nonferrous Metals Industry Corp under a 30-year deal has arrived in China, an official said on Thursday.
The first shipment of 35,000 tonnes had arrived in China on Wednesday at Qingdao city in the eastern province of Shandong, the China National Nonferrous official said.

Sino Mining Ltd, a subisidiary of China National Nonferrous, signed the agreement with Alcoa last year to buy 400,000 tonnes of alumina a year for 30 years, with an option to increase to up to one million tonnes if needed.
The imports would help China meet a shortage of about one million tonnes a year, the official said.
Alcoa World Alumina is 60 percent owned by Aluminum Co of America and 40 percent by Australia's WMC Ltd.
Under the deal, Sino Mining was to make a lumpsum payment of $240 million to Alcoa World.
China National Nonferrous had so far put $80 million of its own funds in the import project and more than 10 foreign banks had provided $160 million in soft loans, the official said.
China's alumina output reached 465,200 tonnes in the first five months of this year, up 10.3 percent year-on-year, earlier figures show.
